The civilian government, civilian institutions had primary responsibility to secure this area, to conduct investigations regardless of whether the perpetrator was military or civilian, to refer the matter after of an investigation had been completed to the relevant prosecutors, state prosecutor or military prosecutor, and then have the courts process the matter. I again remind the Court that at no point in time did anyone come to General Gotovina and say, "The system is not working. We cannot cope. You need to do something." It didn't happen. Why didn't that happen? Because through the time period of the statistics as you've seen them and the dates of these documents, General Gotovina is in Bosnia conducting an operation known as Operation Maestral. And in early October he is in Bosnia conducting Operation Southern Movement, Southern Sweep. It was understood that General Gotovina could not have too much on his plate. He was conducting offensive operations in a foreign country and these matters were left to other responsible institutions. Your Honours, we submit again in conclusion, General Gotovina was a man who found himself in a circumstance in the late July of 1995 where the Bosnian Serbs were pursuing their end game. This was not introduced to you this morning for purposes of defending or giving evidence about the legitimacy of Operation Storm. This evidence is instead relevant to the state of mind as well as the obligations of General Gotovina throughout the indictment period. You must be aware of what the Bosnian Serbs were doing in Bosnia in July of 1995 because General Gotovina was the one primarily tasked with stopping what was happening in Bosnia in July of 1995 and onwards. You must understand the context that General Gotovina, as Mr. General Mladic said in the video which we showed you, General Mladic said when asked, "Are the Croatian forces now spread too thin?" He said, "I'm not going to answer your question, but wait and see." Who he was talking about was General Gotovina and his forces. General Gotovina throughout this time period is dealing with matters related to Bosnia and, as I said, Operation Storm for him was a left turn, to complete that operation, come back, consolidate his forces and continue on against Mr. Mladic. We respectfully submit, Your Honours that at the conclusion of the Prosecution's evidence you will find that General Gotovina conducted himself at all times in accordance with the laws of war, conducted hostilities at all times in accordance with the laws of war, that there is no evidence of any excessive shelling of Knin. In fact, the evidence is overwhelmingly to the contrary. That General Gotovina issued repeated orders to his subordinates for the respect of the rule of law and discipline. You have seen the video of how energetic he was in insisting upon that, and we believe it is unfair to call that boilerplate orders. Your Honours, we submit to you that the conclusion of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I thought that my body language looking at the clock three or four times would be sufficient for you. Then I started getting all my stuff together, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Not even. We submit to you, Your Honours, at the conclusion of the Prosecution's case you will find that there is no evidence and you will dismiss this case pursuant to Rule 98. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. This concludes the opening statements to the extent the parties wished to make an opening statement. Tomorrow morning we will start hearing the evidence. Mr. Tieger, I take the witness scheduled for tomorrow is available. It might well be that in view of a pending motion that we start tomorrow in private or closed session to further deal with this pending motion than hear the evidence of Witness 136. We adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.
